full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J: This petition for leave to appeal by the petitioner is from the judgment and order of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal dated 13-7-92 in Appeal No. 10 of 1992 dismissing the appeal on the ground of limitation and maintainability. 

 2. The petitioner filed Tribunal Case No. 189 of 1988 before the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka for a declaration that he is entitled to retrospective promotion as Extra Assistant Commissioner of Taxes with effect from 5-10-81 with all financial and incidental benefits. By judgment and order dated 11-12-91 the Administrative Tribunal allowed the Tribunal case on contest. On appeal by the respondents the Administrative Appellate Tribunal held that under Rule 17(1)(c) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 the petitioner was required to file an appeal to the President against the impugned order dated 20-5-86, denying the petitioner retrospective promotion with effect from 5-10-81. The time for filing the appeal is three months from the date of the impugned order, but the Appellate Authority (in this case the President) has the discretion to extend the time by another three months, but the petitioner filed the appeal against the impugned order dated 20-5-86 after 1 year 11 months and 18 days and, as such the appeal was rightly returned to him by the respondents on 20-7-88. The petitioner's appeal being barred and there being no decision of any higher administrative authority in respect of the impugned order dated 20-5-86, the petitioner's application before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation as well as not maintainable. The Administrative Tribunal held that the petitioner filed various Tribunal cases before filing the present tribunal case and, as such, he will get the benefit of section 14 of the Limitation Act. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal repelled this contention and held that section 14 of the Limitation Act is not applicable to proceedings before the Tribunal. 

 3. Mr Asrarul Hossain, learned Counsel for the petitioner, could not show us from the provisions of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 that section 14 of the Limitation Act is applicable to proceedings before the Tribunal. The Appellate Tribunal correctly decided the point.
